descriptionChirho: Adjective in construct (אֶרֶךְ אַפַּיִם) meaning 'slow of anger, long-suffering, patient', a standard divine epithet describing God's forbearance. Found in the foundational theophanic formula of Exod 34:6 and its numerous echoes: Num 14:18, Neh 9:17, Ps 86:15, 103:8, 145:8, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2, Nah 1:3. Also applied to human patience in Prov 14:29, 15:18, 16:32. In Jer 15:15 with preposition ל meaning 'in/by Your patience'. Multilingual glosses confirm the 'slow/patient' meaning: arb طويل (lit. 'long'), deu 'langsam/slow', fra 'patient/longueur', hin धीरज/दीर्घ, kor 느린/더딘, spa 'lento de'. All auto-split clusters represent the same adjective in this construct phrase.

Adjective meaning 'long' in physical or spatial sense, describing extent or dimension. In Ezek 17:3 the great eagle is described as אֶרֶךְ הָאֵבֶר 'long of pinion', referring to the physical length of wings (paralleled by גְּדוֹל הַכְּנָפַיִם 'great of wingspan'). In Eccl 7:8 אֶרֶךְ־רוּחַ 'long of spirit' means patience/endurance, but the underlying adjective retains its spatial 'long' semantics applied metaphorically. Glosses show arb طويل 'long', deu Länge, hin लंबे/लम्बी, kor 길다/김, spa 'larga/largo'. Distinct from the 'slow of anger' formula which is a fixed theological epithet.
